_doc: 20 §1 (audio direction), §3 (the 12 music tracks), §4.1–§4.6 (the SFX families), §5 (technical spec). One row per audio asset slot. 🔒 Counts are transcribed, never reconciled: any disagreement with doc 20's stated totals is recorded in `discrepancies`.

direction.palette: Acoustic and orchestral-lite: plucked strings, hand percussion, marimba, soft brass, choir pads. Avoid synth leads and EDM — they fight the chibi art.
direction.musicMood: Adventurous and light in early biomes, tenser and lower in later ones. Never dark or oppressive; this is a cosy grind, not a horror game.
direction.sfxLength: 60–400 ms for combat and UI, up to 1.2 s for celebratory stingers
direction.frequencyDiscipline: Combat SFX live in 200 Hz–6 kHz where phone speakers actually reproduce. Nothing important below 150 Hz.
direction.loudness: Music −18 LUFS integrated, SFX peaks at −6 dBFS. Music ducks 6 dB under the crit and level-up stingers.
direction.silence: The board has no music bed during the roll wind-up — 0.4 s of near-silence before the die lands makes the landing hit.

technical.sfxFormat: WAV 16-bit 44.1 kHz mono in source, converted to OGG q4 for shipping
technical.loopPoints: Music loops must be sample-accurate. Verify by looping 20× and listening for a click.
technical.naming: mus_ and sfx_ per the manifest, snake_case
technical.busStructure: Master → Music / SFX / UI, each with its own volume setting
technical.ducking: Music −6 dB for 0.5 s under sfx_crit, sfx_levelup, sfx_boss_phase, sfx_merge_success
technical.adHandling: Full audio duck to silence before any ad, restore on return. Mandatory — nothing is worse than game music fighting an ad.
technical.polyphonyCaps: Combat hits capped at 6 simultaneous voices with a 30 ms retrigger guard, or a fast build becomes a wall of noise
technical.memory: Music streamed, SFX fully loaded. Total audio budget < 40 MB.

promptScaffolds.music:
{MOOD}, fantasy mobile game background music, light orchestral with
{INSTRUMENTS}, warm and melodic, medium tempo, loopable, no vocals,
no drums-heavy EDM, clean mix, cheerful chunky character,
suitable for a cute chibi adventure game
promptScaffolds.sfx:
{DESCRIPTION}, short game sound effect, punchy and clean, cartoon fantasy
game audio, dry, no reverb tail, mono, no music

totals._doc: Counted from the id lists, not copied from doc 20's stated totals. ⚠️ Doc 20 claims 94 SFX and 106 combined; eight dice-family rows are gone with the die's special faces and the reroll (sfx_die_land_star/surge/fortune/void/chain, sfx_reroll, sfx_nudge, sfx_face_upgrade), so the shipped register is 86 and 98.

discrepancies.claim: SFX length: 60–400 ms for combat and UI, up to 1.2 s for celebratory stingers
discrepancies.observed: sfx_victory is a 'triumphant 1.5 s fanfare' (1.5 s)
discrepancies.detail: §1 caps celebratory stingers at 1.2 s; §4.3's victory fanfare is 1.5 s. Both are transcribed as written.

discrepancies.claim: 60–400 ms for combat and UI, up to 1.2 s for celebratory stingers
discrepancies.observed: 8 of 94 SFX state an explicit duration: sfx_boss_telegraph 1.2 s, sfx_campfire 1.0 s, sfx_die_tumble 0.8 s, sfx_levelup 1.2 s, sfx_merge_charge 0.9 s, sfx_mount_summon 0.8 s, sfx_stage_gate 1.2 s, sfx_victory 1.5 s
discrepancies.detail: Recorded as an observation, not a violation. §1's 60–400 ms band is stated over 'combat and UI' without defining which of the six §4 families those are, and 'celebratory stinger' is likewise undefined, so no mechanical conformance check is possible here. The one unambiguous overrun — 1.5 s against a stated 1.2 s ceiling — is DSC_STINGER_LENGTH. The other durations are transcribed as written.

discrepancies.claim: §1 Loudness: Music −18 LUFS integrated, SFX peaks at −6 dBFS. Music ducks 6 dB under the crit and level-up stingers.
discrepancies.observed: §5's Ducking row names 4: sfx_crit, sfx_levelup, sfx_boss_phase, sfx_merge_success
discrepancies.detail: §1's prose names the crit and level-up stingers; §5's table adds sfx_boss_phase and sfx_merge_success. ducksMusic follows §5, the more specific of the two.

discrepancies.claim: a prompt descriptor for every sound (§4's scaffold takes a {DESCRIPTION})
discrepancies.observed: 8 SFX carry no descriptor of their own: sfx_hit_light, sfx_hit_medium, sfx_hit_pierce, sfx_hit_slash, sfx_pet_heal, sfx_pet_zap, sfx_ui_toggle_off, sfx_ui_toggle_on. Ids sharing one '·' segment: 20 §4.6: sfx_ui_toggle_on + sfx_ui_toggle_off have none
discrepancies.detail: A descriptor is attached to the id it directly follows. Where a segment holds several ids the earlier ones keep descriptor:null rather than inheriting, so the hole stays greppable. Note that §4.3's 'escalating blunt impacts' reads as covering sfx_hit_light/medium/heavy and 'whoosh with a crystalline pop' reads as belonging to sfx_hit_magic alone — a human ruling, not a transcription.
